questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the dinosaurs disappeared from Earth
That an advanced civilisation came before us
How scientists look for life on other planets
How fossils are made over millions of years
questions.why: They discuss the Silurian hypothesis: an advanced civilisation before us that left no trace.

questions.q: What do Phil and Beth think about life on other planets?
options: Phil believes in it, but Beth doesn't
Neither of them believes in it
They think scientists have already found it
They both think it probably exists
questions.why: Phil says there are so many planets there must be life, and Beth agrees.

questions.q: Why was Adam Frank so shocked during his conversation with Gavin Schmidt?
options: Gavin asked how he knew there was no earlier one
Gavin said he had found an alien civilisation
Gavin showed him a very strange fossil from Asia
Gavin told him the Earth was younger than he thought
questions.why: When Adam said there'd been no other civilisation, Gavin asked 'How do you know that?'

questions.q: What does the Silurian hypothesis suggest?
options: Humans originally came from another planet
Dinosaurs built cities and roads long ago
Traces of a very old civilisation couldn't be found
The Earth will be destroyed quite soon
questions.why: It says if such a civilisation existed hundreds of millions of years ago, we couldn't find traces.

questions.q: Why does Adam say fossils won't help prove the hypothesis?
options: Fossils are too hard and expensive to dig up
Little life fossilises, and it wasn't there long
Almost all old fossils have been destroyed
Most scientists don't trust fossils anymore
questions.why: He says only a tiny fraction of life is fossilised, and 10,000 years is too short to create many.

questions.q: Why do the presenters mention plastics and concrete?
options: To show how the Earth's crust is formed
To warn listeners about plastic pollution
To show an old civilisation would leave marks
To explain how fossils are made in rock
questions.why: Our plastics and concrete will last very long, so critics say an earlier civilisation would leave similar marks.

questions.q: How does Adam respond to people who disagree with him?
options: He ignores them and carries on with his work
He says they don't understand science at all
He changes his mind immediately
He welcomes their work; it leads to agreement
questions.why: He says others affirm or push back, and after 20–40 papers 'you have a consensus'.

questions.q: What is Phil's personal view of the idea?
options: It's so mysterious it's OK to keep an open mind
It's definitely true, and he's sure of it
It's a complete waste of scientists' time
It has already been proven wrong by experts
questions.why: Phil says the idea is so mysterious, 'it's OK to keep an open mind'.
